subject: cardboardRobot
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
Style: cardboard craft.
reasoning:
I'm planning the overall structure of a cardboard-box robot costume for a kid, thinking through a cardboard craft aesthetic with foil, bottle caps, and tape, then sketching out a body skeleton with hips, spine, chest, head, arms, and legs to keep the design manageable but detailed.

Working out the proportions and coordinates: a box helmet with a face opening to show the kid's skin, cardboard-tube arms wrapped in foil, jeans and sneakers for legs, and rough height measurements for ankle, knee, hip, chest, and head placement. Writing helper functions for box geometry...

Defining more joints...

Finalizing the arm positions: shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand points plotted along a bent curve. I'm covering the upper arm with a sleeve sweep in the shirt color, then wrapping a cardboard-roll "foil tube" effect around it for the armor piece.

For the hands, I'm using a skin-colored sphere at the wrist tip, considering whether to add simple finger capsules or keep it as a basic palm shape for the kid's hand.

Defining the leg chain joints...

For the pelvis I'll use a jeans box mostly hidden under the cardboard torso box, which sits centered around chest height with roughly 0.46 width, 0.42 height, and 0.32 depth, open at the bottom with dark arm-hole discs on the sides. I need to watch the box's top edge against the helmet's bottom so they don't overlap—settling on torso top around 1.03 and helmet bottom around 1.0.

For the helmet, I'm placing it around y=1.17 with dimensions roughly 0.32 wide, 0.3 tall, 0.3 deep, built from five thin panels (left, right, top, back, bottom) leaving the front open except for thin strips framing a square face hole, sized about 0.17x0.17 and centered near y=1.13 so the skin-colored head sphere underneath peeks through at the right depth.

Now I'm layering on cardboard-craft details: tan tape strips, darker corrugation edges along cuts, a marker-drawn chest control panel with bottle-cap buttons in red, blue, and yellow, dials, a glowing green screen, a lightning bolt, a heart sticker, a pipe-cleaner antenna with a pompom ball, foil-covered cup ears, and a text label like "ROBO-KID" rendered via an SVG texture on a plane.

I'm placing the textured panel plane just in front of the torso box face, then working out angled flap details on top of the box using rotated thin boxes hinged outward to suggest folded cardboard flaps, figuring out the rotation math so the outer edges lift upward correctly.

I'm checking whether the raised flaps would collide with the helmet's bottom edge, and adjusting the torso box height and flap angle so the helmet sits cleanly on the shoulders without clipping.

For the torso coloring I'm picking cardboard tan with a darker edge and tape highlight, and considering adding subtle stripe-based corrugation texture with low contrast to suggest the cut cardboard edges.

I'm also planning the shipping marks like "THIS SIDE UP" and "FRAGILE" labels plus arrows, and settling on a compact palette: cardboard tones, tape beige, foil grays, and bold accent colors (red, blue, yellow, green) alongside ink and skin tones, keeping the total under the color limit.

Still refining palette...

Building out the spine joint chain...

Adding helper functions for spheres, then building out the face details on the head and jaw bones -- shaping the skull, chin, and a small mouth element at lip level.

Now I'm computing eye placement, figuring out the sphere surface coordinates on the head so the eyeballs sit correctly at the right depth and offset.

Still placing facial features...

Still defining helmet panels...

I'm thinking about adding a thin outline frame around the hole edges using dark ink-colored strips to suggest a cut border, then moving on to helmet details like a small antenna rod bending upward from the top.

For the antenna, I want a red catmull-spline sweep with a yellow pompom ball at the tip, possibly zigzagged for a coiled look. I'm also planning cup-shaped foil cylinders for ears positioned on either side, each with an inner dark ring accent, and considering a small glowing red LED detail near the antenna base on the helmet.

Now I'm sketching out an RGB light strip on the helmet front using three small colored cylinders, plus a tape strip detail across the top and corners. For the torso, I'm settling on box dimensions centered around the chest with a defined waist-to-hip span, then laying out front, back, and side panels with gaps left for arm holes.

Side panels need circular cutouts around x ±.23 where the arms exit near the shoulder-to-elbow path — I'm placing a dark disc there to simulate the cut edge, sized slightly larger than the arm tube radius so a visible ring shows without weird overlap. I'm also checking whether the shirt collar should peek out near the neck at y 1.0 given the shoulder position.

Now I'm building the interior body: shirt shoulders inside the top opening, a torso shirt box, pelvis/jeans box near the hips, and a front control panel with a bezel and a glowing waveform screen on the chest.

Adding button caps and dial details...

I'm skipping the stitched seam idea and focusing on practical trim: darker edge strips at the four vertical corners, plus "FRAGILE" labels on both sides as text planes facing outward so they're readable from each direction.

For the back, I'm adding a sticker-style "FRAGILE" warning and "THIS SIDE UP" arrows as a texture, and considering small decorative foil-tube rocket accents near the top back corners, though I need to work out their attachment depth against the box's back face.

Now I'm placing foil-wrapped tube geometry for the arms, defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions, and sizing the upper and forearm tube segments with rim caps and tape-band wraps for a cardboard-robot aesthetic.

Working out the hand geometry now, placing the palm at the wrist joint and building fingers as four capsule shapes spread across a local axis, with a ball used for the elongated palm shape.

Fingers spread along z with thumb angled forward at the corner, so I'll place finger offsets stacked along z and skip treating digits as separate chains for simplicity. For legs, I'm setting up a chain per side with hip, knee, and ankle joints positioned relative to the hip socket.

For the leg sweep, I'm using a tapered radius function for jeans-colored tubes down each leg, adding a rolled cuff ring at the ankle, then layering a white sock tube and shoe geometry on top.

For the shoe itself, I'm building a white sneaker body with a toe cap, a red sole box positioned so its bottom sits at ground level, laces as small ink-colored boxes, a sole stripe, a rounded toe ball, a heel back piece, and a red velcro strap.

I'm wrapping the shin in a cardboard-textured box with foil cuffs and tape bands at top and bottom, keeping it positioned above the ankle and below the knee joint. I'm skipping the belt since it'll be hidden, then adding a skin-colored capsule bone connecting the neck to the head.

Now I'm working on the label textures using SVG, making sure to properly escape the XML and add "FRAGILE" text.

Writing screen SVG code...

Setting up the lightning bolt extrusion shape, checking that the outline points don't self-intersect to keep the geometry valid.

Checking that edge D-E doesn't cross B-C confirms the polygon stays non-self-intersecting. Now I'm setting up the extrusion orientation, figuring out which axes face front versus up so the thickness extrudes correctly in the z-direction, placing this at the right z-depth with a thin yellow ink layer underneath.

Now I'm moving on to other parts: scaling up the ink outline underneath, then designing the dial with a foil cylinder and pointer, a ring of small tick marks placed around an arc using rotated boxes, and bottle caps made from nested cylinders with a ridge detail.

I'm also positioning the box panels — bezel, back label, and side/front/back hinged flaps rotated outward at angle, sizing their width and depth, and leaving out the corrugated edge detail and considering whether to add crossed tape strips on the front panel.

Now I'm adding small gold brass brad details at the helmet and torso corners, plus wire-loop ears and a few marker-drawn designs on the helmet sides. For the face, I'm building a smiling expression with a row of small white teeth boxes arranged in an arc below the eyes.

I'm adding a white teeth box above the lower mouth, then setting up a separate jaw bone with its own skin-toned geometry positioned below the head. For the head sphere itself, I'm limiting it to only the upper portion so it doesn't overlap the jaw piece, calculating the phi range to find where the rim should cut off.

I'm sketching a helper for mirrored left/right loops with side suffixes, confirming that lerp and polyline helpers accept array-based vectors, and setting up the arm chain rig with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints parented to the chest, then sweeping a tapered shirt-colored tube along it.

Now I'm working through the leg chain parented to the hips, and detailing glove and cuff geometry at the wrist using small colored tube segments layered over the forearm. I'm also setting up THREE.Vector3 math to compute direction vectors between wrist and elbow for positioning these cuff and sweep radii accurately.

For the fingers I'm using capsule shapes anchored to the tip joint, then moving on to the antenna, which I'm building as a zigzag Catmull-Rom spline with a small red tube radius, topped with a yellow pompom ball and a tiny foil-cap cylinder base, bringing the total figure height to about 1.54 units.

I'm now placing gold brad fasteners at specific coordinates on the helmet front strips and torso corners, keeping part count manageable around 200, and adding foil crinkle details as small bands and rings at tube ends.

Writing foil tube helper...

Still working out tube lengths and lerp positions for the upper arm, elbow joint, and forearm segments to position the foil wraps correctly.

Using leg.tip! for the ankle, with the shin box bone keyed to the knee joint spanning knee to ankle, so thigh jeans stay visible. Shoes get positioned at foot x = s*.075, and I'm checking whether to add a tape-cross detail on the torso front center control panel.

Jeans cuffs and socks get rod geometry positioned relative to the leg's x and bone joints, with the lowest grounding point at the sole bottom set to zero. I'm also defining a helper function P that wraps part creation with bone, position, and extra options, plus setting up SVG text labels with font-family and adding glow effects for screens and LEDs.

For typing, I'll just use `any` for bone references rather than fighting TypeScript's strict mode over object types.
